clue.text: A nuisance, like the North Wind

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome person or thing, a nuisance
as means like, in the same way as

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a cold northerly gale is a real pest.
explanation.walkthrough: BOREAS is the Greek god of the North Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Boreas is the god personifying the cold wind from the north.

clue.text: One school! of thought in the plot is divided

indicators.note: in places the person and the doctrine group inside the patch of garden

parts.note: a plot of ground in a garden, such as a flower bed
I is the Roman numeral for one
a sect is a group following one doctrine, a school of thought

explanation.surface: A remark that a single philosophical camp has split over the storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' tempts as a story's plot; here it is a garden bed. The exclamation mark is as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bisected has been cut into two halves, so it is divided.

clue.text: Starts again producing abstracts

definitions.meaning: picks up again after a pause
résumés are summaries or précis of a longer text

explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning continues after a break, and a noun for written summaries, spelt alike.

clue.text: The great band-leader?

parts.note: points both to the Macedonian conqueror called the Great and to Irving Berlin's song about a ragtime band led by a man of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great led armies, and Alexander's Ragtime Band gives a namesake who leads a band.

clue.text: Look in to get free meat

indicators.note: in tells us the word for look sits inside the word for breaking out

parts.note: to escape is to get free
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone told to pop in and pick up some complimentary meat.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a thin boneless slice of meat, often veal, beaten flat and fried.

clue.text: Armed alliance to regularize foreseeable issue

definitions.text: Armed alliance to regularize foreseeable issue

parts.words: Armed alliance to regularize foreseeable issue
parts.note: a marriage made under threat of a firearm to make an expected baby legitimate

explanation.surface: Sounds like a military pact drawn up to settle an anticipated problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring and 'armed' is literal: the bride's father holds a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurried marriage forced because the bride is pregnant, jokingly enforced at gunpoint.

clue.text: Heretic with an air of guile

indicators.note: something done with guile is crafty, so the letters are slyly rearranged

explanation.surface: A dissenter is described as having a cunning manner about him.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange AN AIR. An Arian follows Arius, who denied that Christ was equal to God the Father.
explanation.definitionFit: Arianism was condemned as heresy by the early Church, so its follower is a heretic.

clue.text: Casual labourer tails off

indicators.note: tails means follows behind, so the worker comes after the other word

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A temporary worker's shift is tapering off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tails off' reads as dwindling; here 'tails' says the worker comes behind, not that something fades.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual and unconcerned.

clue.text: He deserves to be paid

parts.note: someone who earns money has merited the wage, read literally as one who earns

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain worker has a right to his wages.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is one who earns, and to earn is to deserve payment for work.

clue.text: Writer who gave his son lines conditionally

definitions.text: Writer who gave his son lines conditionally

parts.words: Writer who gave his son lines conditionally
parts.note: the poem If, addressed to the poet's son, is a string of conditional lines

explanation.surface: An author passes verses to his boy, but with strings attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conditionally' refers to the poem If—, each stanza beginning 'If you can...'; 'lines' also hints at a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of the Jungle Book wrote the poem If— as advice to his son John.

clue.text: Players' instruction sent out so loosely

indicators.note: loosely suggests the letters are let go and set down in a slack new order

explanation.surface: A direction to musicians was dispatched in a rather careless way.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SENT OUT SO. 'Players' are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Sostenuto is a musical direction telling performers to sustain the notes.

clue.text: Reason there's a number missing in Dante's work

indicators.note: missing means the abbreviation for number is dropped from the title

parts.note: the Inferno is the first part of Dante's Divine Comedy
no. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a canto has dropped out of the Italian epic.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce, to reach a conclusion by reasoning.

clue.text: Fellow-member joining any Army Group?

parts.note: a companion, abbreviated comp., is a fellow member of an order
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a comrade may enlist in any army formation.
explanation.walkthrough: COMP. is a standard abbreviation for companion, as in an order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is an army unit, a subdivision of a battalion; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: This gives Hull the edge, upsetting NW League no end

indicators.note: upsetting means the letters are knocked over and set down in a new order
no end means the final letter of league is lopped off

explanation.surface: A Hull team gains an advantage by toppling a north-western league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the Yorkshire city but is a ship's hull. 'No end' cuts LEAGUE to LEAGU, and 'upsetting' rearranges NW with LEAGU.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a boat's side.

clue.text: Relieved daughter after rest

indicators.note: after places the daughter's letter behind the word for rest

parts.note: ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A parent is relieved once his daughter has had a lie-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means relieved, as pain or worry is lessened.

clue.text: Traitor gets degree — an anomaly

indicators.note: an anomaly is something out of line, so these letters fall out of their order

explanation.surface: A turncoat is somehow awarded a university qualification, a strange irregularity.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts his side or cause, so he is a traitor.

clue.text: What may be achieved by some bighead?

definitions.text: What may be achieved by some

parts.note: big gives great
a ness is a headland, so head gives ness

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a conceited person might accomplish.
explanation.walkthrough: Echoes Twelfth Night: 'some are born great, some achieve greatness'. 'Bighead' looks like a conceited person but is split into its two halves, big and head.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line says some people achieve eminence by their own efforts.

clue.text: Wind from point to point on trackway

parts.note: west is a point of the compass
E for east is another compass point
RLY is the abbreviation for railway, a way of tracks

explanation.surface: A breeze blows from one spot to another along an old track.
explanation.definitionFit: A westerly is a wind blowing from the west.

clue.text: Indian church retains her agreement with English

indicators.note: retains means the church letters hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A Native American congregation keeps her on, with the consent of an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people, called Indians in older usage.

clue.text: It's hard to put up these lights at top speed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the little word is written upwards

parts.note: foot completes footlights, the lights along the front of a stage

explanation.surface: Someone finds it difficult to install stage lighting in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These lights' points to FOOT making FOOTLIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotfoot means in great haste, as fast as one can go.

clue.text: Flyer well below par

definitions.meaning: a large bird of prey that soars
in golf, a hole completed in two strokes under par

explanation.definitionFit: Both a big raptor and a golf score two strokes better than standard.

clue.text: One of a shoal of fish?

definitions.text: One of a shoal of fish?

parts.words: One of a shoal of fish?
parts.note: a large sea fish, and playfully anyone belonging to a group

explanation.surface: Asks what a single member of a school of fish is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouper is a large sea fish; read literally it is one belonging to a group, like a shoal.

clue.text: Finally drag rubbish to a cave

indicators.note: finally picks only the last letter of drag

parts.note: rot is nonsense, another word for rubbish

explanation.surface: In the end someone hauls junk into a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave, often picturesque.

clue.text: Pest-controller on an old bicycle

parts.note: a device for catching vermin, also the name for a toothed pedal on old bikes

explanation.surface: A rat-catcher doing his rounds on an ancient bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattrap catches rodents, and rattrap pedals were the serrated metal pedals of old bicycles.

clue.text: It's right to like new poet

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it proper to admire a modern poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was a German-language lyric poet.

clue.text: Tried to put down wrong in Carmen's city

indicators.note: put down wrong means the letters are written out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An attempt to belittle an opera heroine in her home town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TRIED TO. 'Carmen' is not Bizet's heroine but car men: Detroit is the Motor City.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the centre of the American motor industry, home of carmakers.

clue.text: Giant Scandinavian fish

definitions.meaning: to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.definitionFit: Both an ogre of Norse legend and a verb for angling with a trailed line.

clue.text: Boniface as river-guard?

parts.note: the Inn is a river flowing through Austria and Bavaria
a keeper is a guard or custodian

explanation.surface: Asks whether a saint might serve as a watchman on a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: Boniface is the landlord in Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem, so the name means a publican.
explanation.definitionFit: Boniface became a generic name for a landlord of a pub or hotel.

clue.text: Exit sounds to be the more important

indicators.note: sounds tells us the word for exit is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: an exit is a way out, here put as out way

explanation.surface: Departure noises are judged to matter more.
explanation.definitionFit: To outweigh is to exceed in value or significance.

clue.text: A second carrier is missing

parts.note: a tray carries things

explanation.surface: A tray that held something has gone missing for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Astray means gone off course or lost, so missing.
